description: Experiment C (embedding backlog): after a bounded settle (both queues empty, worker at 0, no scaling activity in progress), N existing documents of researcher-profile-v1 (the first N unique keys in the scan order of the DynamoDB ArtifactRegistry table; the latest registry version of 20 of them checked first; M-01: no S3 Vectors data-plane call from the laptop) are enqueued as embedding-task-v1 messages for re-embedding under their existing keys and metadata. Observes the embedding queue depth (visible, in flight), the worker service's desired, running and pending tasks every 15 s, the worker alarms and the actual scaling activities, throughput, retries (received vs deleted), the embedding DLQ against its baseline (not 0 after F) and the drain and scale-in times. The spec gate needs at least one worker scale-out and one scale-in (0 -> 1 -> 0); 0 -> 1 -> 2 -> 0 is the extended objective. N = 19,200 and the wait limit 5,500 s are final (6c, decision 11.4, from infra-engineer's 5a timeline and rag-engineer's handler rate). Runs at the session 2 build commit and the D3 plan; thresholds, cooldowns and maximums are never changed for it.
datasetSnapshot: dblp-2026-11-01 (DBLP XML with dblp.dtd), subset rule dblp-subset-v1 (datasets/dataset-manifest.yaml); the researcher-profile-v1 vectors of the Phase 14 export run=f2625d504b12749389cf4f5b1a26aed4

resourceLimits.terraformSource: infra/terraform/modules/runtime/variables.tf (worker_max_count 2, worker_scale_in_minutes 5) and autoscaling.tf (worker_out step +1, cooldown 120 s; scale-out alarms on both queues, 60 s, >= 1; scale-in alarm on the sum of visible and in-flight of both queues, 5 of 5, breaching); infra/terraform/modules/workflow/variables.tf (embedding_max_receive_count 5, embedding_visibility_seconds 300); config/course.json embedding.requestsPerMinute 300, tokensPerMinute 1000000, batchSize 64; worker embedding-loop concurrency 2 (ServiceLimits.EmbeddingWorkerConcurrency, services constant, no config key)

notes: APPROVAL: the human signs this exact file at D9 with the line APPROVED-MANIFEST-SHA256: HEX64 in docs/agent-runs/phase-15/approvals.md; any change is a new sha256 and a new approval (6c set N and the wait limit before D9, so nothing is signed yet). FINAL N = 19,200, wait limit 5,500 s (6c). ONE-TASK RATE (estimates, not measured): rag-engineer's handler rate per receive loop (one SQS receive of up to 10 messages: 1 GetVectors, per task GetItem + GetObject + PutItem, 1 Voyage call for the 10 texts, 1 PutVectors, receive and acknowledgements; agent-report-rag.md 'Handler one-task rate') is low 2.4, central 5.4, high 10 tasks/s; the worker runs 2 embedding loops per task (service-engineer: ServiceLimits.EmbeddingWorkerConcurrency = 2), so one task drains low 4.8, central 10.8, high 20 documents/s (ceiling per task: Voyage 300 requests per minute x 10 texts = 50/s). TIMELINE (infra 5a, estimates): first scale-out t0 + 1-3 min (SQS metric delay, alarm period 60 s); the first task receives at t0 + 2-5 min; second scale-out at the first + 120 s cooldown, t0 + 3-5 min; the second task runs at t0 + 5-7 min. N RULE (decision 11.4): N >= (time to the second scale-out + 3 min) x one-task rate x 2, with the upper end t0 + 5 min: (300 + 180) s x rate x 2 = 4,608 (low), 10,368 (central), 19,200 (high); N = 19,200 meets the rule under the high rate and is under the 20,000 cap; researcher-profile-v1 holds 64,090 documents (Phase 14 rag report), so 19,200 keys can be selected. KEY SELECTION (changed in repair-01, finding M-01): the vector bucket policy (infra/terraform/modules/vectors/main.tf, DataPlaneOnlyForRuntimeAndOps) explicitly denies ListVectors and GetVectors to every principal except the query, worker and ops task roles, so the laptop profile's list-vectors and get-vectors (the 6b/6c design, decision 11.4's mechanism) would be refused in the run and in --preflight. Orchestrator decision, no security change: the collector never calls the S3 Vectors data plane. It selects keys from the DynamoDB ArtifactRegistry table (Terraform output dynamodb_table_names.ArtifactRegistry; no resource policy; storage TableSpecs.ArtifactRegistry: pk artifact#vector#INDEX/VECTOR_KEY, sk v#NNNNNNNN, append-only, one item per registered version, written by the vector ingest after PutVectors). RULE (repeatable): a read-only, eventually consistent Scan with FilterExpression begins_with(pk, 'artifact#vector#researcher-profile-v1/'), projection pk only, 1,000 items evaluated per request, at most 1,000 matches per CLI call continued with --starting-token, at most 80 calls and 420 s between calls; duplicate pks (several versions of one key) dropped keeping the first; the first N unique keys in scan order are taken; fewer than N: exit 3, nothing sent. Scan order is the table's partition order (the same for unchanged contents, not guaranteed after repartitioning), so the selected keys and their sha256 are recorded (selected-keys.txt, tool-record selection.keys_sha256). CHECK (replaces the 20-key vector-metadata sample): for 20 evenly spaced selected keys, the latest registry version (Query pk = key, ScanIndexForward=false, Limit 1) must hold textHash, embeddingModel and embeddingDimensions, with model and dimensions equal to config/course.json; any miss: exit 3, nothing sent. The vector metadata itself (the handler's required keys) is checked by the handler: a missing field is a permanent failure of that task, counted as a workload failure (worker-outcomes.csv permanent-failure), never hidden. TWO-TASK SCALING UNCERTAIN (still true, for a reason the rule does not model): the rule assumes all N messages are visible at t0, but the collector sends them sequentially, one AWS CLI send-message-batch call per 10 messages (1,920 calls; about 0.7 to 1.5 s per call on the laptop, estimate, not measured), so the enqueue takes about 20 to 45 minutes at about 7 to 14 messages per second. When the first task starts (t0 + 2-5 min) the backlog is about 840 to 4,200 messages; under the low and central rates (4.8 and 10.8/s, at or below the send rate) it lasts past the second scale-out; under the high rate (20/s) it shrinks by about 6 to 13 per second and can empty around t0 + 3 to 6 min, near the second scale-out, after which visible depends on the sends still arriving. The gate (0 -> 1 -> 0) does not depend on it; 0 -> 1 -> 2 -> 0 is the extended objective and is reported as observed. DRAIN TIME (upper bound, low rate, one task): 19,200 / 4.8 = 4,000 s (about 67 minutes) after the first task starts; central: about 30 minutes at one task, in practice bounded by the 20 to 45 minute send phase. WAIT LIMIT (from the first send): first task start allowance 300 s + drain at one task under the low rate 4,000 s + scale-in (5 min at zero + alarm lag + task stop, about 540 s, infra 5a: 6 to 9 minutes) + 10 min = 5,440 s -> 5,500 s (the send phase, at most about 2,700 s at 7 per second, is inside the drain at the low rate). maxDurationSeconds 7,700 = settle 900 + selection (the ArtifactRegistry scan, bounded at 420 s between calls, expected 1 to 3 minutes, plus 20 latest-version queries) up to about 500 + wait 5,500 + scaling activities and worker log counts 360 + 440 margin. COST (estimate, COSTS.md rates): central about $0.12, upper bound under the low rate about $0.25: Voyage about 1.7 M tokens (about 88 tokens per document, Phase 14 estimate; inside the free allowance, $0), S3 Vectors PutVectors about 115 MB logical upload (about $0.02), DynamoDB about 19,200 GetItem and 19,200 PutItem on demand (about $0.02 to $0.04), S3 GETs about 19,200 (under $0.01), SQS about 1,920 send calls plus receives and deletes (under $0.02), the worker (1 vCPU, 2 GB, about $0.04 per task-hour) at up to 2 tasks for up to about 1.5 h (up to about $0.12), worker log ingestion about 5 MB and the metric export (negligible); the ArtifactRegistry key selection (M-01; estimate): a scan is charged on every item evaluated, filtered or not; upper bound one full-table scan per selection: describe-table (aws-api, repair-01; DynamoDB updates these sizes about every 6 hours) shows about 251,000 items and about 205.5 MB, so 205.5 MB / 4 KB = about 50,200 read units at strong consistency, halved for an eventually consistent scan = about 25,100 read request units, at $0.125 per million (COSTS.md, on demand) about $0.003 per selection; the D9a --preflight repeats the selection once, so about $0.006, plus 20 one-item queries per selection (negligible); costBoundUsd 0.5. METRICS: SQS series of the embedding queue, its DLQ and the job queue seen in account (aws-api list-metrics, 6b); AWS/ECS CPUUtilization, MemoryUtilization, LiveTaskCount with ClusterName and ServiceName seen in account for the three ALB services (the worker's series is not listed yet because it has not run in the retention window; an empty series stays missing); DynamoDB query-session consumed capacity seen in account. Task counts: the collector's describe-services samples and scaling activities (Container Insights is off); CPUUtilization sample counts are not used as task counts. LIMITATIONS known in advance: re-embed write rate is the rate of the re-embed path only, not of a first ingest; concurrent duplicate deliveries are not observable (both count processed); the worker log line (event reembed-delivery, keys taskId and outcome, values processed, replayed, permanent-failure, transient-failure, stream prefix worker/) was checked in 6c against the rag and service handoffs and matches the collector constants; the handler's permanent failures during C are workload failures (bad selected documents), not worker failures.
